approach: In `run_job` (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs), the `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm (line 1537) gives the job-limit slot back: take `self.st()` and set `st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1)` before pushing the line and returning `RunStep::NeedsAccepting`. `st.begun` and the money (the cost already added by `st.budget.add(run.cost)` at line 1527) are left alone. The JobLimit check (1433), the increment (1439) and the passed, held and failed arms are untouched. A new integration test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs uses the existing `Stub` with `needs_accepting: vec!["a"]` and `max_jobs: 1`. Docs, `--job-limit` help and CHANGELOG are updated. The producer runs the new test with the decrement temporarily removed and with it restored, and quotes each command and its output in the report. The criterion 5 checks (fmt, clippy, workspace tests) are run as separate commands after the fix is restored, each quoted with its result.

decisions.choice: Give the slot back in the `needs_accepting` arm of `run_job`, by decrementing `st.started` under the state lock.
decisions.reason: `st.started` (incremented at drain.rs:1439) is the one counter behind the JobLimit check (1433), the approval room check (1889), the fill-plan check (2008), the read-ahead room check (2555) and the restart `jobs_left` (2896). Fixing the counter at the arm fixes every reader at once. Only `Run.needs_accepting` (set at 3572) reaches this arm, so failed, held and budget-short outcomes are unaffected.

rejected.option: Special-case the JobLimit stop reason or skip the limit check when it would stop the drain.
rejected.why: Treats the symptom. The counter stays wrong for read-ahead and restart, which read `started`.

rejected.option: Increment `st.started` only after the run result is known.
rejected.why: The slot must be taken before the read and run so concurrent workers cannot exceed the limit. It would restructure admission, far more than one focused change.
Whether the re-read ends as needs accepting is known only after the run. A re-read that does not need accepting should still count as a job.

decisions.choice: Use `saturating_sub(1)` and leave `st.begun` and the budget accounting alone.
decisions.reason: The re-read's cost must still count against the money budget (out of scope to change). `begun` records that money was held for the item, which stays true.

rejected.why: Changes budget-hold semantics, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Drive the test through the existing stub `needs_accepting` run result, not `Source::Reread`.
decisions.reason: The reading accepts this. `run_job` reacts only to `Run.needs_accepting`, whatever produced it, and the seam exists (tests/drain.rs:89 and 223). The existing test at 1305 uses the same route.

rejected.option: Build a new stub that returns `Source::Reread` through the stale-reading path.
rejected.why: Needs read-ahead and concurrency setup and adds no coverage of the counter.

decisions.choice: Show the old-counter failure by running the new test with the decrement temporarily removed, and quote the commands and outputs in the report.
decisions.reason: Job 20261103-193428-df2m was rejected for citing no command for criterion 2. The verifier has no stash or checkout, so the report must carry the recorded output.

rejected.option: Only describe the assertion that would fail.
rejected.why: This is the exact failure of the earlier job.

decisions.choice: Demonstrate criterion 5 with three separate whole commands (fmt, clippy, workspace test), each with a stated failure mode and the cargo toolchain as seam.
decisions.reason: The verifier may run only whole simple commands, so `&&` chains are replaced by separate runs. The criterion's value is that the new code and test do not break the checks Athena itself runs.

rejected.why: Not a whole simple command; the verifier cannot run it.

steps: Read `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop` (tests/drain.rs:1422), `a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure` (1305) and the stub's `needs_accepting` handling (89, 223). Grep tests/drain.rs for `urgent` to find the urgent-queued-request test.

risks.risk: The decrement could run when the slot was not taken, so `started` underflows or the limit is exceeded.
risks.mitigation: The arm is reached only after the increment at drain.rs:1439 in the same call, so the decrement exactly undoes it. `saturating_sub` guards against underflow.

risks.risk: With several workers, a worker may meet the JobLimit check while `a` is in flight and end its own item with JobLimit before the slot comes back.
risks.mitigation: This is the existing behavior for a full limit; the fix targets the sequential case in the criterion. The producer notes the limit in a comment and does not widen the change.

risks.risk: The report again cites no command for criterion 2, or none for criterion 5, as happened in job 20261103-193428-df2m.
risks.mitigation: Steps 4, 5 and 7 require each command and its output to be copied into the report; a report line without a command and output counts as not done.

risks.risk: The test passes for the wrong reason, for example `b` is blocked by something else.
risks.mitigation: The test also asserts the log has `run a`, `run b`, `land b`, and that `a` stays in `report.queued`. The old-counter run must fail on this test only.

risks.risk: The temporary removal of the decrement is left in the tree.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 restores it and checks with `git diff` that the decrement is present; criterion 3 reads the final diff.
